pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test 'AC-1' asserts all three seed rows are 0 and that value 2 is rejected.
src/index.js item() prefixes '★ '; test 'AC-2' checks starred and unstarred rendering.
WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id; test 'AC-3' stars 3 and 1 and expects id order.
Test 'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all both list all items in id order.

The code implements the links, but the last commit (8df3855) renamed the test from 'AC-5: each views links...' to 'each view links to the other'. No test names AC-5 now, and the spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review'. By the rule, an item that no test names is unmet.
Object.hasOwn guard returns 400; test 'AC-6' covers Starred, none, empty and __proto__, and checks that no <li> is listed.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'; test 'AC-7' asserts it. The checker script now accepts a query.

findings.what: The follow-up commit 8df3855, titled 'Follow-up edits' and authored by a bot, removed the 'AC-5:' label from the test that proves the item. The item is now named by no test. The PR also says 'Changed after the go: nothing' while a commit after the go touched acceptance traceability.
findings.fix: Restore the title 'AC-5: each view links to the other'.

findings.what: The PR body's 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing' don't mention the late test rename. The checker's route regex was also loosened. That is disclosed, so this is minor.
findings.fix: After restoring the label, keep the PR body accurate about the follow-up commit.

lenses.note: A spec exists; the implementation matches its decisions (in-place order, query parameter).
All 4 state-table rows have tests. AC-5 lost its test label in the last commit.
The tests assert behaviour and would fail on wrong code. I did not run them; CI runs them on every push. The traffic test fake and the checker tests were extended, not loosened.
The README mentions ?show=starred; that is enough.
The 400 guard uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ is safe. The SQL is a fixed string chosen from a whitelist. No defects found.
The query value is only used as a lookup key in a whitelist. Titles are HTML-escaped. No planted instructions were found.
The diff has only a minimal server-rendered HTML link and no UI files such as CSS or components.
The diff has only a minimal server-rendered HTML link and no UI files such as CSS or components. The PR gives no preview.
The title is accurate and under 72 characters. 'Changed after the go: nothing' is slightly inaccurate given the follow-up commit.
